subject: Business Models
title: Amazon: Store to Platform to Cloud
description: A short lesson to help you apply Amazon: Store to Platform to Cloud.

hook.text: Amazon started selling books. Its most profitable unit is now cloud computing. That's a triple pivot.

buildup.text: Amazon went from bookstore to everything-store to marketplace (third-party sellers) to cloud infrastructure provider.

discovery.text: AWS started as internal infrastructure. Amazon realized it could sell excess capacity to other companies.

twist.text: AWS generates more operating profit than Amazon's entire retail business combined. The side project became the core.

climax.text: Amazon's willingness to pivot repeatedly—and bet on adjacencies—created a $1.5 trillion company.

punchline.text: Books to cloud servers. Amazon's best business was an accident.

quiz.question: How did AWS originate?
options: Amazon sold excess internal infrastructure capacity
A competitor forced them to build it

details.summary: Amazon evolved from an online bookstore to a third-party marketplace to the world's leading cloud computing provider. Each layer built on the previous one: retail infrastructure powered the marketplace, and internal technology tools became AWS, now generating the majority of operating profit.
details.whyItMatters: Amazon shows how internal capabilities can become external products. AWS was built to solve Amazon's own scaling problems and became a 90 billion dollar business. This pattern of productizing internal tools is a powerful innovation strategy.
takeaways: Amazon evolved from retailer to marketplace to cloud infrastructure provider
AWS emerged from internal infrastructure built for Amazon's retail operations
Third-party sellers now account for over 60% of Amazon's total unit sales

faq.question: How did Amazon's internal infrastructure become AWS?
faq.answer: Amazon built scalable computing infrastructure to handle peak retail demand. Realizing others had similar needs, they packaged it as web services anyone could rent. AWS launched in 2006 and now generates over 90 billion dollars in annual revenue.

faq.question: Why does Amazon tolerate thin retail margins?
faq.answer: Retail drives customer traffic and data that powers advertising revenue, marketplace commissions, and Prime subscriptions. AWS generates high-margin profit that subsidizes retail growth. Each business reinforces the others in a flywheel effect Jeff Bezos designed intentionally.
